$comment: Hash of each frozen version's slice in the dump it was blessed from, excluding doc/description/examples (none of which reach the generated output), taken off the parsed dump before generation runs (see lib/dump-digest.mts). Generation fails if a frozen version's slice moves, because its files are skipped and the rest of the tree would be generated against a model they no longer hold. Run `yarn generate:api` and paste what it prints to seed a version. Record $source when you do.
$source: ghcr.io/truenas/middleware:master, middlewared 20261001001317~truenas+1 (digest sha256:708acd6d2e6a574314dbb7b91d9a53e08d9d9522c8ad6dee41f5aaa83bb39ab8, fetched 2026-10-01). Everything the 2026-09-16 seed recorded still holds and is not repeated here; what follows is what moved. The dump itself got smaller: middleware stopped emitting v24.10, v25.04.0, v25.04.1 and v25.04.2, so it carries 8 version slices where the 2026-09-16 dump carried 12. All four are below --min-version v25.10.0 and nothing generated from them, so this changes no output; it is recorded because a future run that wants an older version can no longer get it from master's dump. **As in the previous seed the frozen files do not move with the hashes, and for the same reason.** Two things differ in substance from the 2026-09-16 dump across all six 25.10 slices, and both are event payloads: sharing.s3.query's SharingS3Entry gains tier (bringing TierInfo and ZfsTierRewriteJobEntry with it) and its multipart_etag default moves from COMPOSITE to MINTED; zpool.query's ZPoolVdev gains stats_ex. Neither method exists at 25.10 -- v25.10.0 declares no s3.* or sharing.s3.* method at all, and none of its 741 methods reaches ZPoolVdev -- so this is the unfiltered-event leak and nothing else: the events carry the running tree's models because middleware adds them with no version filter. Regenerating would import master's shapes into a released version's types; the files stay as their marker says, and only the hashes follow the dump. Unlike the 2026-09-16 seed this needs no hand-maintained aliases: because no 25.10 call-side model reaches SharingS3Entry or ZPoolVdev, leaving the files frozen produces no divergent payload type inside a frozen version, so there is no PoolDatasetEntryInput-style correction to carry. New at v26.0.0: sharing.s3.recover and sharing.s3.recoverable_buckets (with SharingS3RecoverBucket, SharingS3RecoverableBucket and SharingS3RecoveredBucket). SharingS3Entry gains tier on the call side, which splits the event payload off as SharingS3EntryInput -- the same leak, but at a version where the call side is real, so the divergence is genuine and typed rather than hidden. truenas.license.info moves: LicenseFeatureEntry loses source and LicenseInfoEntry gains issued_at. ZPoolVdev gains stats_ex here too. New at v27.0.0: webshare.config and webshare.update are re-declared because WebshareEntry and WebshareUpdate gain mcp_enabled, mcp_allowed_groups and mcp_allow_write (and v27 now imports v26's Passkey for them). One thing in this dump cannot reach TypeScript at all and still mattered: config.save's ConfigSave.secretseed default moves false -> true at v27.0.0. The emitted ConfigSave is field-for-field identical at v25.10.0 and v27.0.0, because an optional boolean carries no default. Generated against the generator as it stood at 8880738 this evicted config.save from ApiJobDirectoryBase -- 'config.save' extends JobMethod<BaseApiDirectory> went from true to false -- because canonical() counted the flip as a structural change, re-homed ConfigSave at v27, and an entry hoists into a base directory only while every type it references is chain-stable. That is fixed in the commit this seed is stacked on: the shape comparison now ignores assertions the emitter does not render, so the flip moves nothing and config.save stays in the base. Worth knowing separately from the types, because none of them can say it: at 27.0.0 config.save() with no arguments now includes the secret seed in the backup.
